As someone who's played way too much roguelike deckbuilders, who's 100% Slay the Spire twice and Balatro once, I will say this is one of the better games in the genre out there. It wears its inspirations on its sleeve but has its own unique mechanics. It's high difficulty caught me off guard because it's implemented in a way that feels like losing was a skill issue and not RNG (an issue that games such as 9 Kings at high difficulties and Dog Witch suffer from). It isn't a walk in the park, and there's enough content for multiple playthroughs (not as much as the aforementioned greats in the genre but it just came out so what can you expect). The gameplay loop is satisfying, there are multiple approaches to winning, and the high difficulty is refreshing. Anyone who's played a lot of any other games in the genre will love this game. It is so good that the negative reviews were frustrating to read. "The game is too hard", "The game is too much like Balatro but worse". These lowbrow reviews made with 2 hours on record make me wish for the writers to live a happy life with a loving family and a lamp. The game is good. It innovates in its own unique way that does not feel heavily RNG-dependent or boringly easy. Would recommend.

Engaging Deck-Builder, Limited Market Depth Insider Trading is an interesting market-themed roguelike deck-builder with meaningful resource and tempo management. However, its market model feels fundamentally unidirectional. There is no sustainable short-selling mechanism; market crashes mainly serve as setups for long entries rather than independent profit strategies. Over time, gameplay revolves more around deck optimization and resource control than actual market reasoning. The card effects lack strong causal links to real-world financial logic, limiting transferable insights. If you enjoy strategic deck-building and resource optimization, this is worth trying. But if you're expecting deeper, multi-dimensional market simulation, it may feel constrained. Overall: solid as a deck-builder, limited as a market model. ---------------------------------- 有趣的卡牌遊戲，但市場維度受限 《Insider Trading》作為市場題材的 roguelike 卡牌遊戲，設計本身是有趣的，也確實比一般卡牌遊戲多了一層資源與節奏管理的思考。 但它的市場模型本質上是單向的。 遊戲幾乎沒有可持續的放空機制，下跌更多只是為了低檔做多的準備，而不是獨立的獲利策略。 最終，核心玩法更偏向卡組優化與資源管理，而非真正的市場判斷。卡牌效果與真實金融邏輯缺乏因果連結，較難形成可遷移的交易思維模型。 如果你喜歡策略構築與資源管理，這款遊戲值得一試； 但若期待更深層的市場模擬與多維度交易機制，可能會感到受限。 總評：作為卡牌遊戲不錯，作為市場模型仍有成長空間。
在猴子面前巴菲特简直是个新兵蛋子。74w%收益率是什么东西啊，还有-100%出了新手模式直接给经济干崩溃了。

It feels mid. There is clearly a lot of effort put into this game, but gameplay wise it's too dependant on good rng to be truly enjoyable and there aren't many tools at your disposal to mitigate that. Building a coherent deck, one that gets you the price increases/decreases you need to survive, is extremely difficult. Not only are you forced to constantly expand your deck, but you are also dealt different types of cards each week which only synergise with themself. It is somewhat possible to mitigate this, but you still end up with a deck that is at least 50% garbage. If you end up with a working deck it isn't because of what you did, but because of the lucky rolls you got. Wins feel unrewarding because of that, and loses even more frustrating because there wasn't anything you could've done differently. True to its roguelike origins it does a horrible job of explaining anything except the bare minimum. Which is okay in principle, but there are things, like the short mechanic, that aren't explained at all. Figuring those things out by yourself however is impossible to do with all the factors at play. Have fun playing The Hand. Maybe I'm not seeing it, that is always a possibility, but then again I'm not surprised if I don't because of how convoluted and random everything is. Addendum: So I tried giving this game a few more chances to convince me, but the more I play it the less I like it. Most cards have drawbacks that seem to vastly outweigh their benefits so there is no incentive to take anything apart from bears/cubs and bulls/calves. Perks/Curses feel useless or are so edge-casey they might as well be useless. And to add insult to injury, you have to buy the perks before you actually get to see whats available. I never saw any reason to take anything else except the same 4 perks. That is if I was able to afford anything, because thanks to the game consistently dealing extremely chaotic queues I constantly had to spent my tokens on fixing those or I'd end the day with just +/- ~2%. But then again, perks made no difference at all as I still ran out of gas week 3 no matter what. The games rng just won't give an inch in that regard as is perfectly demonstrated by the weekly events. They are going to prevent whatever you're trying so hard, they might as well just outright end your run there and now. So, as sad as it sounds, but for the moment I'd stay away from this game until the rng has been toned down and/or the games balance isn't as harshly stacked against you as it currently is. The music is nice, tho.

The demo was fun, but the released version isn't. For instance, if you have a goal to make X money in a week, there is no incentive or benefit of making more money than X. And each new week, your money is reset to $1000 regardless of whether you made 1 million the week before, but the targets are almost exponentially harder week after week. And sure, perks help every week, but those two become insanely expensive week after week, so not even in the easiest difficulty can you really have fun. Oh, and birds are broken. Want to destroy the game balance? Get birds. If not, reset and try again. Such a shame.

While I am a huge fan of Balatro and the roguelike genre, the core of Insider Trading with adjusting price in both directions was more confusing than rewarding. While excited for this unique element of gameplay of "red = not always bad", I could not put a synergy together in a meaningful way. I can possibly blame my Steam library of simplistic roguelikes for maybe why I couldn't get on a legitimate run in this game, but either way, the replayability faded quickly. I couldn't piece together a strategy or synergy that worked in my favor. I appreciated the effort between incorporating consumables, perks, etc, but compared to a game like Balatro, the shop phase felt extremely bland. With most cards offering similar % increases/decreases and some cards offering unique abilities, there wasn't enough there to get excited over. As some reviews mentioned, it felt extremely RNG-dependent and channeling a deck in different ways netted to a similar outcome with gains/losses equating out to a similar result. All in all, I could be missing a key piece to what makes this game stand out, but it wasn't for me.

作为一个加密货币，股票交易者，我今晚一口气玩了 10 小时通宵。必须承认：很上头，节奏快、反馈密集、每局都想再来一把。 但如果你是冲着“交易/金融模拟”来的，我觉得完全不沾边。 本质更像 卡牌构筑 + 肉鸽跑分：核心在于凑牌、叠 combo、滚雪球，k线只是包装盒。你更多是在算牌序和倍率，而不是做交易决策（比如仓位管理、风险控制、信息博弈、情绪周期那种）。 玩久了会有一种空虚感：爽是爽，但意义不大，也很难给我带来任何真实交易的启发。我现在就非常后悔自己浪费了这么多脑力和精力在这样一款游戏上。 不过如果你并不是抱着模拟交易的心态来玩，我相信你也能找到你的乐趣点。 ps：简体中文翻译有些问题，不过不影响游玩，需要猜一下。

Its a conflicting game. This game has a really interesting idea with it being a deckbuilder roguelike but with the stock market. The game is set up to be kinda like balatro, but is made to be nowhere as fun or satisfying to play and beat like balatro is. The biggest problem being just how over reliant the game is on RNG, especially in the late game when you are getting close to beating the goal, or managing to put together some semblance of a build. It becomes the most infuriating part of this game. One of the more appealing things of deckbuilders is figuring out how to set up synergies and builds to lead you to victory, but this game's RNG puts a huge wrench on that idea and wants you to completely ignore that. The most baffling thing about this game is that winning "too much" on this game will guarantee a loss of the run, and i have no idea why the game was set up that way. The concept is cool and novel, but the execution of the idea leaves a lot to be desired.

A great game for hardcore fans of Balatro and Cloverpit. I've always been amazed when i seen VODs of Balatro or Cloverpit playthroughs where the player can go infinite every time. if this is you, this game is for you. However if you're like me where you struggle through these games, this is not for you, This game requires impeccable strategy, RNG, etc to compete. i struggle to complete it on the lowest difficulty. The main issue is that to win you need to be able to both massively raise, and massively lower, the stock price almost at will. So you need to build a deck that does both, but due to the RNG of drawing cards each round, you may find that your positive and negative cards cancel each other out, or you get mostly positive when you wanted negative etc. Rerolling cards helps but its very common to run out of cash while rerolling before you get a good hand, again due to RNG. You are forced to add cards to your deck but culling is much rarer so its hard to get exactly the build you need, even if you can deduce what to do with the cards you are given. My advice is to save your money and buy another game from the genre, or just try 100% the games from the genre you already have.

I want, so badly, to recommend this game because the potential here is absolutely wild, but, as you'll see a few reviewers saying, there are significant changes that need to be made before I can amend the review. My main reservation here is one simple thing: Skyrocketing the stock price is the best thing this game has to offer in terms of a pure dopamine rush, but you only need to do it once per week (and even then it's not a wise move). The rest of the week you'll just be begrudgingly tanking the stock price and skipping, biding your time before the next week. The super "high score" runs are usually done just as a fun way to end the week: the game will even warn you NOT to trade once you've hit your goal. You are not rewarded AT ALL for huge increases in stock price: seeing those green candles smashing to the moon usually spells disaster for your next few turns. You won't be able to buy the stock the next day because it's too expensive. You'll usually want to beat the goal by a few hundred dollars then rinse and repeat for each week. There are a lot of potential builds, but it's the same song and dance no matter what deck you're running. Insider trading is ABOUT BEING FILTHY RICH, but this felt more akin to being a nervous nerd who doesn't want to be caught with his hand in the cookie jar. Oh, also money means pretty much nothing and the game's econ revolves around tokens. So yeah. If we see money play more of a significant factor, then I would be the first to revise this review, because WOW the art, the ideas, the music, and the concept are INCREDIBLE. I'll be keeping my eye on updates - this could become my favorite deck builder roguelike; it's SO close.

I feel like we need to talk about the vibes of this game. The CRT esthetic, the way the cards activate in rhythm to the music, the satisfaction of lining up a bunch of similar cards and watching them go nuts, all the juice - the vibes are on point. The gameloop is also excellent, but as others have pointed out, it does need more balancing. It feels like a game you can easily "solve" within an hour or two and once you've figured out the best approach, it makes a lot of decisions become no-brainers with several cards becoming too niche or too watered-down to ever really want to pick them up. I'm optimistic that the dev will sort out the balance issues though, so with time, I really don't see it being a concern. And even as is, it's still a fun initial experience figuring out the best options. If you like incremental games like Balatro, this is absolutely worth adding to your library. It's a fresh take on the genre and well worth the price tag.

Do not take any reviews under 2-hours seriously. Your first run alone will take you upwards of 30-mins if you are actually learning each mechanic. Claims of "tanking the stock price to win every round easily" work only in the early levels and the game punishes players for attempting to abuse this past the tutorial difficulty levels. If you are familiar with rogue-like deckbuilders you will have an easy time on your first couple of runs, but the fact that just using a different deck will get you a rare achievement shows that 90%+ of players are not even taking the time to engage with the game in good faith. This isn't Balatro, but Balatro lovers will have a great time with this one. It engages with a similar structure while completely inventing it's own mechanics. It's less luck based which does make it a bit easier at times, but removes some of the frustrations from getting wrecked on a good run by poor RNG. If this get's put on mobile we will see a sizeable drop in worldwide productivity.... please do it anyways :)

This is a remarkably clever game about market manipulation, brinksmanship, and timing. It is NOT Balatro 2, as many of the reviews here seemed to have expected. It is really quite a bit more complicated with tactical decisions at every turn and it is full of tough choices that find you working to figure out how to crash or explode the market -just enough- to come out on top. It is a difficult game with unusual, singular mechanics and as such it does not feel like any of the recent flood of Balatrolikes- it is very much it's own thing. I haven't min/maxed it to death and broken it like some of the more Mentat-minded players here may have so I can't quite speak to whether or not that is actually an issue, but I think most players interested in a compelling investment and stock trading roguelike are going to come out of this happy to have spent the $12 on it. I'm very much looking forward to learning to play it better and getting a promotion!

Is it an interesting game? I suppose so. Does it stay interesting? Sadly no. There is a lot of stuff in here, but the nature of the game does not really encourage you to interact with it deeply. The power disparity between the cards is so extreme that many of them are just not worthwhile to pick up, nevermind keep them. So the experience of the game is that you find one or two cards that are exceptionally strong, and using them your deck becomes strong enough to coast through a week or two with no issue. With that time it is very likely that you can find something strong enough to lower the stock price down to the minimum possible, and then you have essentially won the game. My last run ended when I clicked trade one day then went to take a ♥♥♥♥, when I came back the turn was still running and I closed the game.
